note: Browser performance budgets read by docs/qa/perf-budget.cjs. A budget is a target and is never edited to make a run pass. Known misses are tracked under ratchet (a ceiling the measured value must not exceed while the fix is pending); --ratchet turns a known miss into a regression gate, the default run fails on every miss.

desktop-cable.label: Desktop, cable (25 Mbps, 20 ms RTT, no CPU throttle)

throttled-4x.label: Laptop, 4x CPU, 40 ms RTT, 5 Mbps (same as BLD-045)

phone-low.label: Low-end phone, 6x CPU, 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps, 360x740 touch

ratchetNote: Ceilings = 1.5x the worst scratch-DB measurement seen on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-10 (phone-low clean run 2026-11-10: LCP 8912, INP 1368, switch p95 2727). Server figures come from 5-10 reps on a freshly restarted server, so they are noisy; re-baseline with --probe-reps 30 before relying on them. Lower a ceiling as each fix lands. 2026-11-12 re-baseline (--probe-reps 30, same scratch DB, before then after 162.5): desktop switch p95 264 to under 250; throttled LCP 2920 to 2728, INP 672 to 648, switch p95 928 to 875; /api/v1/inbox p95 330 to 105, p99 400 to 156 (one query for the per-item approval facts); /api/v1/doc/Item p95 165 to 33. Phone ceilings are unchanged: the same build measured 4.8 s to 6.6 s LCP on one machine within an hour, so that profile cannot show a gain this small.
